newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada shares fall after hostile bid.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada shares fall after hostile bid.

text.p: Shares in Gulf Canada Resources Ltd eased on Wednesday after the company announced a C$972-million hostile takeover bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc.
The debt-funded offer was called "unsolicited and wholly unacceptable" by Clyde.
Gulf Canada shares in morning Toronto Stock Exchange trade were off C$0.25 to C$9.30 on volume of 575,564 shares.
Gulf Canada earlier on Wednesday said it planned to offer Clyde shareholders 105 pence per share in cash in a takeover bid valued at 432 million stg (C$972 million).
Edinburgh-based Clyde, which produces about 39,200 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the United Kingdom, Netherlands Indonesia and Australia, quickly urged its shareholders to reject the offer.

Analysts in London said they believed Gulf would be forced to up its offer before closing the deal after Clyde shares on Wednesday rose to well above the bid price, suggesting investors were betting on a rival offer surfacing.

Gulf said it arranged financing for the deal with the Bank of Montreal and was considering a number of options, including C$300 million in asset sales and a C$100 million equity issue, to repay the debt.

Gulf chief executive J.P. Bryan, who has been priming investors for several months on the concept of an international acquisition, told reporters that the company also planned to sell about 20 percent of its Indonsian subsidiary, Asamera.

"It's complicated and the debt question raises its head once again," said a Canadian analyst who asked not to be named. "This million-dollar question on this thing is how much Indonesia is really worth." ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
